extracted.intended_audience: research administrators, grant managers, historians, and researchers consulting historical NSF award records
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and interpret structured award-record fields from a historical NSF listing: PI(s), institution, project title, award identifier, duration, dollar amount, program grouping, and travel/event details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Name(s) of the investigator(s) responsible for the award, shown in LAST, FIRST format; may list multiple investigators separated by commas and 'AND'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'COX, STEPHEN K, AND VONDER HAAR, THOMAS H'; 'KRISHNAMURTI, T N'. Multiple PIs are explicitly joined with 'AND'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution / Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Name of the host institution or organization receiving the award (university, research institute, society, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY', 'UNIVERSITY OF WISCONSIN, MADISON', 'NATIONAL ACADEMY OF SCIENCES'. Often appears immediately above or before PI/project entries and is grouped under a state heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: State / Geographic Grouping Header
rubrics_metrics.description: State or geographic heading used to group award entries (e.g., 'FLORIDA', 'MASSACHUSETTS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'CONNECTICUT', 'DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA'. These are section headers that group multiple institution entries by state or region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project / Activity Title
rubrics_metrics.description: The title or short description of the research, travel, exchange, or support activity funded by the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'REDUCTION AND ANALYSIS OF THE WISCONSIN RADIATION EXPERIMENT DATA COLLECTED DURING BOMEX'; 'TRAVEL TO ATTEND- THE SECOND INTERNATIONAL JOINT CONFERENCE ON ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE'. Titles often indicate purpose (research, travel, exchange, administrative support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award / Project Identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: Alphanumeric award or project code shown in parentheses after the title or PI (e.g., codes starting with letters like A, F, C, followed by numbers and sometimes suffixes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '(A018783 001)', '(F033164)', '(C310197 001)'. Identifiers sometimes include component suffixes (001, 002) and occasional modifiers ('X00', '*').

rubrics_metrics.name: Program / Program Section
rubrics_metrics.description: Top-level program or category under which awards are listed (e.g., 'INTERNATIONAL COOPERATIVE SCIENTIFIC ACTIVITIES', 'INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL PROGRAM', 'COOPERATIVE SCIENCE PROGRAMS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These headings show the programmatic context of entries and group awards by activity type or programmatic initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Purpose / Activity Type
rubrics_metrics.description: Short phrase describing the nature/purpose of the award (research project, travel to attend conferences, exchange of scientists, administrative support, planning/participation in international projects, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'TRAVEL TO ATTEND', 'EXCHANGE OF SCIENTISTS', 'ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES IN SUPPORT OF INTERNATIONAL SCIENCE ACTIVITIES', 'TO CONDUCT RESEARCH'. Purpose often appears in or just after the project title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Period / Duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Length of the award expressed in months or a months value (e.g., '12 MONTHS', '24 MONTHS', '6 MONTHS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '12 MONTHS $36,500', '24 MONTHS $110,000'. Duration is frequently printed immediately before the award amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Dollar amount of the award, presented with a dollar sign and commas (e.g., $36,500).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '$36,500', '$206,700', '$1,400'. Some lines show totals for 'OTHER PROGRAM AWARDS' (e.g., '$104,509').

rubrics_metrics.name: Destination / Event Details (for travel awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: City/country, conference or symposium name, and event dates associated with travel-support awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'MADRID, SPAIN, MAY 11-13, 1972'; 'LONDON, ENGLAND, SEPTEMBER 1-3, 1971'. Travel entries commonly include exact event names, locations, and date ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-award / Component Number
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric suffix or subcomponent identifier appended to the award code indicating subdivisions of a project (e.g., '001', '002').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '(A017822 001)' and '(A017822 002)' represent separate components or phases under the same base project number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Markers / Flags in Codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Asterisk (*) or other code modifiers (e.g., 'X00') appended to identifiers indicating special statuses or internal annotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '(A032589 X00)'; some entries include '*' after program codes. The listing does not define them but consistently shows these markers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative / Multi-PI Indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting that signals collaboration or multiple named participants (multiple PIs, joint projects, or combined institutional tasks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'MARTIN, DAVID W, AND SIKDAR, DHIRENDRA N'; 'REED, RICHARD J, AND WALLACE, JOHN M'. Use of 'AND' and multiple names indicates collaboration or co-investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative / Support Award Designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries that denote non-research grants for administrative services, planning, or support of international activities rather than direct research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES IN SUPPORT OF INTERNATIONAL SCIENCE ACTIVITIES SPONSORED BY THE NATIONAL SCIENCE FOUNDATION (C374000 011)'; these entries typically have larger dollar amounts and describe support roles rather than scientific research.
